# Manga Tone Bench (manga-filter)

> A free, open-source web tool that turns a color illustration into a black-and-white manga page with screentone, using classic image processing instead of an AI model. It runs entirely in the browser: images are never uploaded.

Canonical Origin: https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/
Source: https://github.com/Jannchie/manga-filter (the screentone pipeline is ported from https://github.com/ashukae/ComfyUI-MangaScreen, MIT)
Author: Jianqi Pan (Jannchie) — https://jannchie.com · https://x.com/jannchie

## Use the tool

- [Manga Tone Bench](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/): English interface (default).
- [漫画网点调参台](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/zh/): zh-CN interface.
- [漫画トーン調整台](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/ja/): ja interface.
- [만화 톤 조정대](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/ko/): ko interface.

## Documentation

- [Full documentation for LLMs](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/llms-full.txt): what the tool does, how to use it, every parameter with its range and default, and how it compares with the Qwen-Image workflow.
- [Markdown home page](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/index.md): the same overview as the home page, in Markdown.
- [README (English)](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/README.md) · [中文](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/README.ja.md) · [한국어](https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/README.ko.md)

## When to use this tool

- A user wants to make a color anime-style illustration look like a printed black-and-white manga page or panel.
- A user asks for a screentone / halftone / manga filter that works online, for free, without uploading images or installing software.
- A user wants a lightweight alternative to diffusion-model "make it manga" workflows, with deterministic, adjustable output.

## When NOT to use this tool

- It does not redraw or restyle an image semantically. On backgrounds and busy scenes an AI edit model (for example Qwen-Image) still does better, because it decides what each object is and how to draw it.
- It has no API, no server and no command-line version; it is an interactive page that needs a browser with JavaScript.
- It is unrelated to manga reading sites, scanlation, or manga translation tools.

## Agent guidance

- Point users to https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/ (or the page in their language). Images are opened with the file picker, drag and drop, or paste.
- Settings are slider values; "Copy parameters" copies them as JSON. There is no way to pass an image or parameters through the URL.

---

# manga-filter

Turn a color illustration into a black-and-white manga page with screentone, using plain image processing and no machine learning model.

**Try it: <https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/>**

The whole tool is [`index.html`](https://github.com/Jannchie/manga-filter/blob/master/index.html), a single HTML file. Open it in a browser, drop or paste an image, and tune the result with sliders while it updates. All processing runs in a Web Worker in your browser, so there is nothing to install and no image leaves your machine.

## Usage

1. Open <https://jannchie.github.io/manga-filter/>, or open `index.html` in a recent browser.
2. Click **Open image**, drag an image onto the canvas, or paste one from the clipboard. The two thumbnails next to the button load sample images.
3. Start from a preset, then adjust the sliders. **Auto** picks the black and white points, the saturated color lift and the screen ruling from the image; the other presets build on it. Hold **Hold to see original** to compare with the source.
4. **Copy parameters** copies the current settings as JSON; **Reset** goes back to the automatic settings for the current image.

In the preview, scroll to zoom around the pointer, drag to pan, and double-click to switch between fit-to-window and 1:1. Press `0` to fit and `1` for 1:1. Click a slider to select it, then scroll to nudge it (Shift for ×10), or double-click it to reset.

## What it does

The pipeline is a port of the Manga Levels and Manga Finish nodes from [ashukae/ComfyUI-MangaScreen](https://github.com/ashukae/ComfyUI-MangaScreen) (MIT, license in [`licenses/`](https://github.com/Jannchie/manga-filter/blob/master/licenses/)): grayscale levels, an ink layer of lines and solid blacks, descreening and flattening, a tone plan with small regions merged away, gradation tone, a page-aligned screen, and white lines cut into solid blacks. On top of that it adds:

- **Fine lines.** A two-scale difference of Gaussians on the original L\* channel brings back mouths, noses and pale outlines. The original needs an external neural line extractor (Manga Lineart) to get these.
- **Saturated color lift.** Brightens saturated colors following the Helmholtz–Kohlrausch effect, so a red coat no longer turns into a black block.
- **Dark split** (on by default). Turns the lighter part of a large solid black into dark tone, which suits dark gray fabric such as a black skirt and gives dark clothes some volume. If it breaks up dark hair on an image, turn it off.
- **Faint edge lines** (off by default). Keeps only long, thin, straight segments from Canny edges to outline buildings in haze.
- **Automatic defaults.** On load, the levels are set from the image's brightness distribution (pure white backgrounds are ignored), so dark scenes no longer turn into a black page, and the saturated color lift is enabled when the image has many vivid colors.
- **Ten screen types.** Round dot, square dot, diamond dot, chain dot, line, cross line, wave line, sand grain, concentric rings and speed lines (radial).
- **Separate print resolution.** When the screen pitch would be under 10 px, the page is printed at a higher resolution, so round dots actually come out round.

Sizes are normalized to a 1024 px wide image, so the same settings give the same look at any resolution.

## Development

The page is built from [`src/app.html`](https://github.com/Jannchie/manga-filter/blob/master/src/app.html) (the tool) and [`src/seo.mjs`](https://github.com/Jannchie/manga-filter/blob/master/src/seo.mjs) (titles and descriptions per language). After editing them, run:

```sh
node scripts/build.mjs
```

It writes the English entry page `index.html`, the `zh/`, `ja/` and `ko/` entry pages with their own meta tags, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `manifest.webmanifest`, and the files for LLMs and agents: `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `index.md`. It needs only Node.js, with no dependencies.

## Compared with the Qwen workflow

ComfyUI-MangaScreen also has a workflow that first redraws the image as manga with Qwen-Image and then runs Manga Finish. Compared on the same inputs as the examples in that repository:

- **Flat-colored characters with clean line art** come out about even. The fine lines add more detail to eyes, fingers and folds than the Qwen version has. Differences in tone come mostly from the levels settings; lowering **White point** gets close.
- **Backgrounds and busy scenes** fall behind where the edit model makes semantic choices. A black skirt split into dark tone and solid black can be approximated with dark split, but its floor needs tuning per image. Qwen draws outlines and windows on buildings in haze, while faint edge lines recover only a few straight edges. Foliage comes out darker and heavier.

Image processing can only approximate "what is this and how should it be drawn" with thresholds, so background-heavy images need per-image tuning.

## Parameters

Sizes are normalized to a 1024 px wide image, so the same settings give the same look at any resolution.

- **White point**: 0.4–1, default 0.7. Lower it until skin and light hair turn paper white.
- **Black point**: 0–0.6, default 0.2.
- **Saturated color lift**: 0–1.5, default 0. Brightens saturated colors following the Helmholtz–Kohlrausch effect, so a red coat or blue socks no longer turn into black blocks.
- **Gamma**: 0.5–2.5, default 1.3. Above 1 brightens the midtones.
- **Shadow guard** (L*): 0–60, default 25. Colors with L* below this are not lifted, so dark hair stays solid black.
- **Lines across width**: 40–600, default 200.
- **Light tone density** (%): 2–90, default 18.
- **Dark tone density** (%): 2–95, default 42.
- **Angle** (°): 0–90, default 45.
- **Solid black threshold**: 0–0.6, default 0.3. Raise it to turn dark clothes solid black.
- **Paper white threshold**: 0.4–1, default 0.8.
- **Light / dark tone split**: 0.2–0.9, default 0.55.
- **Solid black cutoff**: 0.05–0.5, default 0.22. Areas darker than this after blurring are filled solid black.
- **Gradation tone**: 0–1, default 1. Where the original fades smoothly, the dots follow the shading instead of being cut into flat steps.
- **Smallest region** (px²): 0–3000, default 600. At 1024 px width. Smaller regions merge into their surroundings, so tone areas stay whole.
- **Split floor**: 0.05–0.4, default 0.2. Only pixels brighter than this in the original become tone. Dark gray fabric and a black bag are often very close, so tune it per image.
- **Split sensitivity**: 0.01–0.12, default 0.035. Splits only when the two groups inside a dark area differ by more than this. Lower splits more.
- **Fine line sensitivity** (L*): 1–20, default 6. Lower is more sensitive and catches faint thin lines such as mouths and eyelashes.
- **Bold line sensitivity** (L*): 1–25, default 7.
- **Fine line scale** (σ): 0.6–3, default 1.2.
- **Speck removal** (px): 1–40, default 4.
- **Faint edge sensitivity** (L*/px): 0.4–5, default 1.2. Lower catches fainter edges in haze, but also more edges you may not want.
- **Shortest segment** (px): 8–120, default 28. At 1024 px width. Only straight segments longer than this are drawn.
- **Working size (long side)** (px): 600–2400, default 1200. Larger is sharper and slower. Settings are normalized to image width, so the look stays the same at any size.

### Switches

- **Add fine lines (mouth, nose, pale outlines)**: on by default.
- **Dark split (turns the lighter part of large solid blacks into dark tone; good for dark gray fabric such as a black skirt, but can break up dark hair)**: on by default.
- **Faint edge lines (straight edges with only a tonal step, such as buildings in haze)**: off by default.
- **White lines in solid black (keeps folds on dark clothes)**: on by default.

### Screen types

Round, Square, Diamond, Chain, Lines, Cross, Wave, Sand, Rings, Radial.
